items.stem: A component uses ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush. You mutate an object's property in place without changing its reference. What happens to the view?

options.text: It may not update, because OnPush checks input reference identity
options.rationale: Correct: OnPush relies on reference changes; in-place mutation can be missed.
That is default change detection, not OnPush.
No error is thrown; the view simply may go stale.

options.text: It triggers a full application re-bootstrap
options.rationale: Change detection never re-bootstraps the app.

items.explanation: Correct: OnPush relies on reference changes; in-place mutation can be missed.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Angular dependency injection are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A service providedIn 'root' is a single app-wide instance
options.rationale: Correct: root providers yield one shared singleton.

options.text: Providing a service in a component creates an instance scoped to that component tree
options.rationale: Correct: component-level providers scope the instance to that subtree.

options.text: Every injected service is always a global singleton
options.rationale: Scope depends on where it is provided.

items.explanation: Correct: root providers yield one shared singleton.

items.stem: Which binding syntax listens for a DOM event and calls a handler?

options.rationale: Square brackets are property binding, not event binding.
Interpolation renders a value; it is not for events.
The hash defines a template reference variable.
